passage:
The school bus was twelve minutes late, and Jeevan had a meeting at nine. As they waited in the drizzle, Binita, eight, said, "Papa, Kiran uncle from swimming gave me a phone to play on. He said don't tell you. Is that okay?"
Jeevan's heart thudded. He kept his voice gentle and crouched beside her. "Thank you for telling me, beta. You did exactly the right thing. You're not in any trouble."
"Are you angry?"
"Not with you. Never with you for telling."
The bus pulled up. Jeevan waved it on. He texted work that he would be late, walked Binita home, and made two calls from the kitchen: to her mother, then to the swimming club's safety officer. Binita sat beside him with her juice, swinging her legs.

qa.q: Who did Binita say gave her a phone to play on?
qa.a: Kiran uncle from swimming gave her a phone to play on.

qa.q: What was Jeevan feeling when he heard about the phone?
qa.a: He felt alarmed, his heart thudding, but kept his voice gentle so Binita would not feel she was in trouble.

qa.q: Which of Jeevan's choices helped Binita most?
qa.a: He thanked and believed her, said she was not in trouble, and acted at once by skipping the bus and calling her mother and the club's safety officer.

qa.q: What might Binita learn from how Papa reacted?
qa.a: She learns that telling is safe and that Papa will protect her, so she is more likely to tell him things again.

grounding: A father on a rushed morning stays calm when his daughter mentions a gift and a secret, thanks and believes her, and acts to protect her that day.

passage:
In her Kolkata classroom, Hansa, ten, lingered by Elizabeth Ma'am's desk. "Ma'am, if someone gives you presents and says don't tell, is that allowed?"
Elizabeth said, "I'm glad you asked me. Can you tell me more?"
Hansa whispered about the tuition bhaiya who gave her bangles and said she mustn't tell her mother. "Please don't tell Mummy. She'll shout at me."
Elizabeth kept her face calm. "Thank you for trusting me. None of this is your fault, and I believe you. I can't keep it secret, because keeping you safe is my job. I'll stay with you."
She sent a student to fetch the school counsellor and stayed beside Hansa until Mrs Rao arrived. By four, with the counsellor present, they had spoken to Hansa's mother, who held her tight.

qa.q: What did the tuition bhaiya give Hansa?
qa.a: He gave Hansa bangles.

qa.q: What was Hansa worried about?
qa.a: She was worried that Mummy would shout at her if she found out.

qa.q: Why was it right for Elizabeth to say she couldn't keep it secret?
qa.a: Being honest while promising to stay with Hansa kept her trust, and fetching the counsellor and speaking to her mother that day protected her.

qa.q: How might Hansa's mother feel at four o'clock?
qa.a: She may be shocked and upset, but holding Hansa tight, mostly relieved that Hansa told someone and is safe.

grounding: A teacher who hears a child mention gifts and secrecy stays calm, thanks and believes her, stays beside her and brings in the counsellor and parent the same day.

passage:
"Abbu, can I tell you something? But you can't be angry."
Rafiq put down his tea. "I won't be angry, Afreen. Tell me."
"The van driver gives me toffees. Only me. And yesterday he said I should sit in the front seat, and it's our secret, and not tell you."
Rafiq felt a hot rush of anger, but not at her. He kept his voice soft. "Thank you for telling me. That was very brave. You did the right thing."
"Am I in trouble?"
"Never. You're not in trouble at all. I believe you."
Afreen let out a breath. "Okay."
"From tomorrow, I'll drop you to school myself." He picked up his phone. "Now I'm going to call your school, right now, so they know."
He called the principal that evening, and the school stopped that driver's route the next morning.

qa.q: What did the van driver give Afreen?
qa.a: Toffees. Only for Afreen.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling when Afreen told him?
qa.a: Rafiq felt a hot rush of anger at the driver, but kept calm so Afreen would feel safe.

qa.q: What did Rafiq do that a trusted adult should do?
qa.a: He stayed calm, thanked Afreen, believed her, said she wasn't in trouble, and called the principal that same evening.

qa.q: How did Afreen feel after her father's response?
qa.a: Afreen felt relieved, letting out a breath once she knew she wasn't in trouble.

grounding: It shows a father hearing his child mention a driver's gifts and secrecy, staying calm, thanking and believing the child, and acting to protect her the same day.

passage:
I'm Sarita, and I've taught Class 5 for eleven years. One afternoon still stays with me.
Uday stayed back after the bell. He said his older cousin gave him new cricket gloves and money, made him do "things he didn't like," and told him to keep it secret. "He says Mummy will be angry with me."
My chest tightened. If I looked angry, he might stop talking forever. So I breathed and knelt to his level. "Thank you for telling me, Uday. I believe you. None of this is your fault."
He cried, and I stayed with him. Another teacher fetched our safeguarding lead, who came straight away. We called his mother to school that afternoon, and before evening the school and his mother had contacted the child helpline.

qa.q: What was Uday's cousin giving him?
qa.a: New cricket gloves and money.

qa.q: How did Sarita feel when Uday told her?
qa.a: Sarita felt alarmed, chest tightening, but stayed calm and breathed so Uday wouldn't stop talking.

qa.q: What did Sarita do that fits a trusted adult's response?
qa.a: Sarita stayed calm, thanked Uday, believed him, said it wasn't his fault, stayed with him, and brought in the safeguarding lead and his mother that afternoon.

qa.q: How might Uday have felt when Sarita said she believed him?
qa.a: Uday likely felt relieved and safe enough to cry, after being told his mother would be angry.

grounding: A teacher recalls hearing a child mention gifts, secrets and pressure from a cousin, staying calm, believing him, and acting that same day.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Wednesday. Written by Sharmila.
In library period, Darshan, Class 6, told me about a "friend" from an online game who sends him game coins and gifts, calls him his best teammate, and has asked for photos "just for him." He told Darshan not to tell his parents or they'd "take the game away."
Darshan kept saying, "Please don't be angry. He's really nice."
I stayed calm, though very worried. "Thank you for telling me. I'm not angry at you at all. You did exactly the right thing."
I informed our safeguarding lead at once, and we called his father in within the hour. His father stayed calm with Darshan, and together we saved the chats and reported the account to the cyber-crime helpline.

qa.q: What did the online friend send Darshan?
qa.a: Game coins and gifts.

qa.q: How was Darshan feeling while telling the teacher?
qa.a: Darshan was worried and scared of getting in trouble, repeating "Please don't be angry."

qa.q: What did Sharmila do that protected Darshan?
qa.a: Sharmila stayed calm, thanked him, didn't blame him, informed the safeguarding lead at once, and called his father within the hour.

qa.q: How might Darshan's father feel on hearing this?
qa.a: His father would likely feel alarmed and protective, but stayed calm with Darshan as the teacher did.

grounding: A teacher records a child mentioning online gifts, a photo request and secrecy, staying calm, thanking and believing him, and acting to protect that day.

passage:
Saturday
Today I told Papa about Coach Vinod. How he gives me chocolates after swimming, and said our talks are a secret, and last week wanted me to stay late alone. I thought Papa would be angry with me for keeping it. He wasn't. He put his tea down and said, "Thank you for telling me, Kashish. I believe you. You did nothing wrong." His voice was soft even though his hands were tight. Then he called Mummy and Mr Shankar, the swimming club's head, and after lunch we all went there together. I don't have to go to class with Coach Vinod anymore. Papa said I can tell him anything, always, and he won't get cross.
I feel lighter.

qa.q: What did Coach Vinod give Kashish after swimming?
qa.a: Chocolates.

qa.q: What was Kashish afraid of before telling Papa?
qa.a: Kashish was afraid Papa would be angry about the secret, and afterwards felt lighter and relieved.

qa.q: What did Papa do that made telling safe?
qa.a: He stayed calm, thanked Kashish, said he believed it and that Kashish did nothing wrong, then called Mummy and Mr Shankar and went to the club the same day.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt inside while staying calm?
qa.a: Papa's tight hands suggest he felt angry and worried, but he kept his voice soft so Kashish would not feel blamed.

grounding: Shows a parent who hears a child mention gifts, a secret and pressure to stay alone, stays calm, believes and thanks the child, and acts to protect the same day.
